claims: The period ladder: 21/21 native CTest targets pass, Visual Studio Win32 Debug, verified 27 August 2026.
The period-pipeline rung compiles softrend and pentprim from upstream and renders dat/sph32.dat as an eight-frame nonblack orbit, final_frame_lit=19284.
The experimental textured path executes but its output is black; completed textured rendering is not claimed.

The rung table names 21 rungs, among them Multi-part assembly: BrModelLoadMany composites the 12-part coupe (claim added 14 October 2026 by the scene-code agent from the same README, pending the author's review).
brender-readme.quote: does not claim completed textured rendering
brender-readme.does_not_prove: x64 or production readiness of the 1998 code; the filling, depth, Gouraud and texture rungs prove the portable C path, not BRender's 1998 assembly path.

claims: ladder64 runs the same 21 programs against BRender 1.4, 64-bit: 21 of 21 pass on 10 October 2026 (Visual Studio 18 2026, SDL3 3.4.16, BlazingRenderer ed5e7a91); CI runs it on every change.
Two documented differences are bridged: BR_COLOUR_RGB's alpha byte, and a 1.4 renderer step that demands over 500 lit and over 500 coloured pixels.

gouraud1971.citation: Gouraud, H. (1971). Continuous Shading of Curved Surfaces. IEEE Transactions on Computers C-20(6), 623-629. doi:10.1109/T-C.1971.223313. Method summary read through Wikipedia, Gouraud shading.
claims: Lighting is computed at the vertices, from normals averaged over the faces that meet there, and interpolated across the face.
gouraud1971.does_not_prove: Gouraud's own formulation; the paper itself was not read.

hecker1995.citation: Hecker, C. (1995-1996). Perspective Texture Mapping, parts I to V. Game Developer magazine. Parts I, II and IV read.
claims: A perspective-correct inner loop does a divide and two multiplies per pixel; removing the divide made the mapper seven times faster in the author's test, and the result looks wrong.
hecker1995.n: one test on the author's machine
hecker1995.quote: seven times faster in my test
hecker1995.does_not_prove: The speedup on other CPUs, or what BRender itself did. The PDFs are for personal reading only: cite and link, do not show the pages.

claims: rosewood.pix is a 256 x 256 INDEX_8 pixelmap with no palette of its own, so load_texture falls back to std.pal, which holds 256 entries.
The centre texel (128, 128) holds index 170; std.pal entry 170 is RGB 99, 24, 24.
rosewood-texel.does_not_prove: What any game drew with this texture; the lookup was read by a small parser that follows load_texture, not by running brview. Added by the scene-code agent on 14 October 2026, pending the author's review.
